issue_context.title: IAcceptResource to maintain Occupance count
issue_context.body:
`ClosestProc` in `OpenRA.Mods.Common/Traits/Harvester.cs` uses quite an expensive query to calculate how much harvesters are already associated with a `IAcceptResources` trait.  It queries all harvesters to see if they are linked to IAcceptResources trait - for each trait. 

An optiomization would be to just maintain an Occupancy count per `IAcceptResources`. Harvesters would have to increment and decrement this value. 

The value indicates how many harvesters are associated with the trait. Allowing the spreading of harvesters over traits/refineries.

Relevant whenever a harvester tries to find a new refinery.
comments: That's part of the plan with the docking refactor. I'm waiting for a few PR's to be merged before I get to optimising it

review_comments: Why is this not part of `INotifyDockClient`?
Because Harvester (nor other clients) are not supposed to inherit it. It'a a notify inferface, meant for trait that wants to be notified

Later in the code you refer to `Contents` as Resources. So it would be better to either rename `Contents` to `Resources`, or change the later `resourceType` var into `contentsType`, to be consistent and avoid any confusion.

I think it would be confusing. Contents - something that is contained / stored. In this case Resources

Anyway that has nothing to do with this refactor

Ok I think this could be its own PR, but just to entertain the point further: In this case I think it should be `contentsType`, because contents can mean anything, yet it is being treated only as resources in the below comment. I actually prefer `contentsType`, because it opens the door for non-resource related contents to be stored (items, weapon ammo, etc.), though if you are doing this you would need an enum specifying which contentsTypes are resourceTypes, so you can then check for this first before handling it with `acceptResources`. If you really wanted you could put a comment stating: "NOTE: All harvester contents are assumed to be resources." or similar, and just leave `resourceType = c.Key` as is, though the former approach would be nicer / more extensible. Anyway I only mention this to raise the issue with the current implementation and provide a potential solution, even if it's not the point of this PR.
As per the prior comment, here this should either be `contentsType`, or the above `contents` dictionary should be renamed to `resources`.
